In NCT02503657, 10 patients took tipelukast 750 mg twice daily and 5 took placebo. FVC fell more on the drug than on placebo (-0.177 L vs -0.025 L), so no benefit was shown. The searches found no human data on tipelukast exposure or on CysLT1 receptor occupancy or blockade at this dose. The company reported lower LOXL2, but LOXL2 is a general fibrosis marker. It is not a direct readout of CYSLTR1 antagonism, and the drug is said to act on several targets, so it does not count as pathway evidence. The triglyceride drop in NCT02681055 has the same problem. No other drug on this target has succeeded in IPF. The bundle cannot tell a drug that never engaged CYSLTR1 from a target that does not matter, so the code is U. The 15-patient trial was too small to answer the question, so F7 is secondary.

The bundle has no direct human exposure, engagement or biomarker data, and no target is recorded. The same intranasal drug met patient-reported efficacy endpoints in social anxiety disorder before the index trial (NCT01217788, NCT02622958; later NCT05011396). That makes the pillars inferred_adequate, assuming the same nasal chemosensory mechanism and comparable dosing. The SAD trials used acute dosing, while the index trial used 28-day use, which weakens the inference. In adjustment disorder, HAM-A change was identical to placebo (-12.5 vs -12.6, p=0.93; NCT04404192), with no tolerability limits, suggesting the mechanism does not drive this disease as tested. The trial was small (n=41) with a large placebo response (F7). Inconsistent SAD results (NCT04754802) and the absence of a recorded target leave real uncertainty (U).

In the conjunctival allergen challenge trial NCT03320434, topical PRT-2761 at 0.5% and 1% did not reduce ocular itching compared with vehicle, while Patanol clearly did. Day 1 redness looked somewhat lower with PRT-2761, but that difference was gone by Day 15, and the posting reports no statistical tests. I found no human data on ocular tissue levels, SYK inhibition or downstream markers such as mast-cell degranulation. The only mechanistic work is a preclinical ARVO abstract with a mouse model and human whole-blood assays run outside the body, which don't count as human evidence. The sponsor gave no reason for stopping. No other SYK inhibitor has succeeded in allergic conjunctivitis, so F1b does not apply. With nothing to show whether the drug reached or engaged its target, the code is U.

The index trial NCT03356639 was a Phase 1 safety, PK and PD study in 32 schizophrenia patients. Its PD measures were Cogstate cognition and EEG P300/MMN. No results are posted, and the bundle gives no stated reason for stopping. The bundle also has no primary target, no other trials, no PubMed abstracts and no same-target comparator drugs. There is therefore no human evidence on exposure, target engagement or pathway effect, and no source explains why the program stopped. Because engagement is no_human_data and nothing separates non-engagement from an irrelevant target or a business decision, the failure is indeterminate (U).

FOL-005 is an osteopontin-derived peptide. One database lists it as an NRP-1 agonist, but the bundle records no primary target. The only binding data come from mouse and human tissue staining (follicle outer root sheath), and the protocol describes these as non-clinical. I found no human measurement of skin drug levels, target engagement or a pathway biomarker. In the intradermal trial NCT03467412, the top dose did no better than placebo. The sponsor reported a gain from baseline, but said the study was 'designed to evaluate the treatment effect versus baseline… not versus placebo' (a minor design point). The topical trial NCT04774874 also failed to beat placebo, and Follicum dropped the alopecia program. With engagement unmeasured, the evidence cannot tell a drug that never engaged from a target that does not matter, so the code is U.

FOL-005 is a modified peptide derived from osteopontin. It has no defined molecular target; it is thought to bind the hair follicle through integrin and RGD-related sites. In the index trial (NCT03467412), the highest dose gave +6.68 hairs/cm2 versus +5.60 on placebo, so the primary endpoint was missed. The sponsor reported a within-group increase but no benefit over placebo. No human data on scalp exposure, receptor binding or a pathway biomarker turned up. The BJD paper reports that high-dose FOL-005 reduced human hair growth ex vivo and in vivo, which suggests some biological activity in hair follicles but does not measure target engagement. No other drug acts on the same target. Because engagement was never measured, the evidence cannot separate a drug that did not engage from a mechanism that does not matter, so the code is U.

The Roche protocol for the AIH trial (NCT04790916) reports human pharmacodynamics. In the healthy-volunteer SAD study WP39826 (NCT03221179, run before the index trial), single doses expanded Tregs in a dose-dependent way: about 2-fold at 2.2 mg, 4-fold at 5 mg and 6-fold at 7.5 mg. The sponsor treated this as the estimated therapeutic range, with little effect on Teff or NK cells. In UC patients in the index trial (NCT03943550), repeated 3.5 and 7.5 mg doses were well tolerated and expanded Tregs up to 5-fold. So the drug reached and engaged IL-2Rα, Treg expansion followed, and tolerability did not limit the dose. Even so, efficacy was below expectations and futility was declared, also ending the AIH program. This means the mechanism was engaged without clinical benefit. Gut-tissue Treg data were not found.

The index AIH trial (NCT04790916) enrolled only 2 patients. It was stopped because the drug fell short in ulcerative colitis (NCT03943550: efficacy trends 'below expectations'), not because of any AIH readout. The healthy-volunteer PK/PD study (NCT03221179) posted no results. One review snippet mentions modest, selective Treg expansion (at most 2-fold) in healthy volunteers. The excerpt does not clearly tie this to RG7835, the full text could not be read, and none of it was in AIH patients. I found no human data on exposure, IL2RA engagement or Treg pathway effects at 7.5 mg in AIH. So a drug that never engaged its target cannot be told apart from a target that does not matter. If the Treg data do belong to RG7835, a target failure carried over from UC (F2) is possible.

The index Phase 3 (NCT03403751) was terminated for 'very slow enrollment of target patient population' after only 58 patients. Its primary endpoint (20/28 vs 23/30, p=0.649) came from an underpowered, early-stopped sample, so the trial could not answer the efficacy question. Safety was balanced, so toxicity did not stop it. The bundle has no human exposure, CD28 engagement or pathway biomarker data. The Phase 1 (NCT01166984) reported only AEs, with no dose-limiting toxicities. The NSTI Phase 3 (NCT02469857) missed its mITT primary endpoint (p=0.135), so it cannot support inferred engagement. The failure is primarily operational (F7). Whether the mechanism matters in sepsis-associated AKI remains indeterminate (U).

K-161 is a Kowa eye drop with no recorded target. Its Phase 2 protocol describes it as an anti-inflammatory, but the target name is redacted, and the drug went straight into the Phase 2 dry eye trial with no Phase 1 study first. My search turned up no human data on drug levels in eye tissue, target engagement or downstream biomarkers. Both the Phase 2 trial (NCT04084483) and the Phase 3 index trial (NCT05403827) missed their sign and symptom endpoints, with results essentially the same as vehicle. No other drug on the same target is listed, and no source explains why the program failed. Because nothing shows whether the drug engaged its target, a drug that never engaged cannot be told apart from a target that does not matter, so the code is U.

Exposure: in the healthy-volunteer SAD study, ASP4345 reached the CSF at levels close to unbound plasma concentrations, which shows it gets into the brain (PMID:32533536). Engagement: there is no human measure of D1 occupancy or potentiation for this positive allosteric modulator, and its binding site is unknown (PMC8182805). Pathway: the Phase 1 MAD study in schizophrenia (NCT02720263, PMID:33203954; 9 patients per dose, 3–150 mg) reported only exploratory positive trends in auditory steady-state response, mismatch negativity and Cogstate tests. The sources treat these as preliminary rather than a clear dose-dependent pathway effect, so I counted them as no adequate human pathway evidence. The index trial missed the MCCB endpoint at 50 and 150 mg, with no tolerability limit on dose. No source explains the failure, and nothing separates a drug that never engaged D1 from a target that does not drive cognition here. Hence U.
